sections.heading: Solution: Move to a Database + Use JDBC

content.text: JDBC (Java Database Connectivity) is an API that enables Java applications to interact with relational databases.

items: Connect to databases (e.g., Oracle, MySQL)
Execute SQL queries
Retrieve and process results
DriverManager: Loads drivers & establishes connections
Connection: Represents the connection to the DB
Statement / PreparedStatement: Sends SQL to DB
ResultSet: Holds returned query data
Use Connection methods:
Always close() the connection once done.
Use Statement or PreparedStatement for SQL execution:
Prevents SQL Injection by using parameterized queries with ?.
Faster performance due to precompilation.
Use {call procedure_name(?,?)} syntax.
Register OUT parameters with registerOutParameter().
Use cursor methods like .next(), .first(), .absolute(n) to navigate.
Use getters like .getInt(), .getString() to access column values.

Close resources (ResultSet, Statement, Connection) in the finally block or use try-with-resources.
Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection.

content.text: A transaction is a group of one or more SQL statements that must either all succeed or all fail together. It ensures data integrity, especially when multiple operations depend on each other.
✅ Commit happens only if all statements succeed
❌ Rollback happens if any one fails

rows: Turns off auto-commit mode so SQL statements are not committed automatically.
Permanently saves all changes made during the transaction.
Reverts all changes made in the transaction so far.

items: Disable auto-commit only when needed: conn.setAutoCommit(false)
Always wrap transactions in try-catch with rollback in catch block.
Always close resources in finally block (or use try-with-resources).
